description: M8 retrieval golden set. Recall@K acceptance for `memhub eval retrieval`. Matchers run case-insensitive substring checks against the recall hit's title and body, so queries survive row-ID shifts and minor wording tweaks. `kind: match` queries contribute to Recall@K; `kind: empty` queries are safety probes that must return no hit that cleared the relevance floor (low-confidence fallback hits are allowed; they are flagged, not vouched for). `kw-` prefixed queries are keyword-bag variants (bare terms, not a question) of existing match targets, and `near-` prefixed `empty` queries are related-but-no-answer probes about topics adjacent to the corpus (issue #225). Two query styles are mixed: keyword-style (3-6 specific terms, ids without a prefix) that play well with FTS5's AND-of-tokens matcher, and `semantic-` prefixed queries written as natural-language sentences that intentionally avoid the durable surface vocabulary — added for re-ranker bake-off (task #20) so headroom exists above the keyword baseline. `doc-` prefixed queries (Wave 4 R10, issue #74) target the doc-chunk ranking path (source_type doc_chunk, gated by the doc floor / include_docs_in_default); `global-` prefixed queries target the machine-global-store ranking path (M9 cross-DB merge, scope=global) — both previously zero-coverage. Every id in this file (base, doc-, global-, semantic-) runs against ONE seeded, hermetic fixture in `tests/retrieval/retrieval_golden_hermetic.rs`, never this machine's live `.memhub/project.sqlite`.

queries.query: how does memhub know an embedding is out of date
queries.notes: Semantic phrasing for decision 28 (content_hash drift detection). Natural 'out of date' vs durable 'content_hash drift' — minimal keyword overlap, designed to exercise a re-ranker. Matcher uses title only because D28's body says 'Mismatch on read marks the embedding stale' without the word 'drift'.

queries.query: why doesn't memhub trust what an agent claims as truth
queries.notes: Semantic phrasing for decision 17 (MCP tool trust split). Natural 'trust what an agent claims' vs durable 'staged writes for claims'.

queries.query: can I move my project memory from one machine to another

queries.query: what does memhub return when nothing matches my question
queries.notes: Semantic phrasing for decision 33 (zero-result behavior). Natural 'nothing matches' vs durable 'Zero-result behavior: empty bundle'. Matcher uses title only because D33's body says 'empty results array' not 'empty bundle'.

queries.query: does reading from memhub leave a trace in the audit log
queries.notes: Semantic phrasing for decision 48 (recall is read-only). Natural 'audit log' vs durable 'writes_log'.

queries.query: what files stay on my laptop and aren't pushed to git
queries.notes: Semantic phrasing for decision 64 (memhub runtime is machine-local). Natural 'stay on my laptop, not pushed to git' vs durable 'machine-local by default'.
Safety probe: gibberish must return an empty bundle, never a hallucinated guess.

queries.query: error handling convention map_err Result propagate
queries.notes: Wave 4 R10 (issue #74): doc-chunk ranking path, previously zero-coverage. Ingested doc auto-enables include_docs_in_default (decision 90); the chunk must clear the doc floor (doc_min_rerank_score) to reach the default bundle this query runs against.

queries.query: what is the convention for returning and propagating errors from a new function
queries.notes: Semantic phrasing of doc-code-style-error-handling — same chunk, natural-language query with minimal keyword overlap.

queries.query: git commit signing key GPG machine
queries.notes: Wave 4 R10 (issue #74): global-store ranking path, previously zero-coverage. This fact exists ONLY in the machine-global store (~/.memhub/global.sqlite, M9) — a pass is only possible via the cross-DB global merge in retrieval::recall, tagged scope=global.

queries.query: what is the default indentation every project on this machine should use unless overridden
queries.notes: Semantic phrasing of the global-store editor-indent decision — exists only in the global store, same global-blend contract as global-fact-git-signing-key.
